rows.basis: Q3 2023 release says Tesla 'more than doubled the size of our AI training compute' for its dataset and Optimus; no AI capex amount for the year is stated. Total FY2023 capex is $8.899B, which is not the AI part.

Only part-year AI figures are stated: AI infrastructure capex of $1.0B in Q1 and $0.6B in Q2 2024; no full-year AI amount. The 10-K says the $11.34B total was 'mainly for AI-related capital expenditures, global factory expansion and machinery', which is the whole, not the AI part. The PP&E note's 'AI infrastructure' category is not used because the model forbids PP&E estimates.

Releases name AI training compute (16k H200 added, Cortex at 67k H100 equivalents; Cortex 2 under construction at Giga Texas). The 10-K says the $8.53B total was 'mainly for global AI and operational infrastructure and factory expansion'. No AI amount is stated, and the PP&E 'AI infrastructure' category is not used under the model.
The Q1 2024 release says Tesla will 'continue to increase our core AI infrastructure capacity'. The 10-K guide is total capex above $11B with no AI amount.

The FY2025 10-K guides total capex 'in excess of $20 billion in 2026, driven by our AI initiatives', and the release plans to more than double onsite Texas compute in H1 2026. The total is the whole, not the AI part. The later cut (over $25B to about $20B) is not broken out by program.
Releases and the 10-K say opex rose 'driven by Cybertruck, AI and other R&D projects'. No AI opex amount is stated.
The 10-K says opex increases were 'primarily driven by additional costs year over year related to AI programs', and Q2 2024 says 'largely driven by AI projects'. No AI opex amount is stated.

The 10-K says R&D rose $1.87B (41%) 'primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs' plus $500M of SBC, and releases repeat 'AI and other R&D projects'. AI is not separated from the other programs, so there is no AI amount.

The Q3 2026 release says 'We expect rising data center demand to continue driving demand for our products' (energy storage). This links revenue to data-center demand in words only, with no amount or share.
